title: Lester Young as a unique person; his father and family
summary: He calls Lester the most unique person he knew and tells of Lester's father and a move to Teddy's house.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: But he took me down to a bar while we were getting measured for uniforms... And he took me down there, one of the few times he took me home. He was a very lonesome person. He was a loner.

Lester Young probably was the most unique person I have ever known in my life. There's never been... I have never had anybody in my life that could come within a mile of him. Playing-wise or talking-wise or dressing-wise or anything-wise, Lester Young was different -- and he was right. I loved that man.

He used to scare me, some of the things he played. He played things that would...just off-the-wall, you know... Like, 'Where did he get that?' I said, 'I can't understand it.' He had a thing he used to play on... [SINGS PHRASE] I think it was 'Sweet Georgia Brown,' something like that. But he used to start it off with 'Poor Little Rich Girl.' WSCHEW!

And the more warmed-up he got, the more the horn would come up, from his father's teaching. You know, his father used to play the saxophone upside-down, you know, at carnival, with the mouthpiece turned around. Did you know that his father taught Ben Webster how to play the saxophone?
Yes, I've heard that. But I didn't know that his father did that upside-down thing.

Oh yeah. That was a thing, you know, to draw people's attention. He never talked about his father. Never once. He never talked about his family. Never. I was at his house, and we had a big fight... I was with Gil Evans and him. And we played records. And some guy downstairs, some relative, started raising hell. And Lester got real mad. He said, 'We're movin' out. We're going to Teddy's house.' And we did. We made about three trips, and we went to Teddy's.
He didn't get along with his father.

That was the first time I ever saw him goof. He reached in his pocket for a cigarette, and he pulled out a bomb. And I said, 'I've finally caught you.' He said, 'Well, as long as you caught me, we might as well smoke it.' So we smoked it, and it was good. And then we spent the rest of the evening together...
Lester Young was probably one of the most unique persons I have ever known in my life. And one of the sweetest, kindest...I quit. Drunk... He was drunk all the time.
